spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is provided explicitly so that "fail gracefully" is an available action
spec_features.evidence: Tool defined in sandbox.py:100-114 (default_tool_specs), dispatched as control in Sandbox.execute sandbox.py:160-165 (CONTROL_TOOLS={'submit','give_up'} at :119), and honored as a stop in runner.py:162-164 (`if control_hit == 'give_up': stop_reason = StopReason.GAVE_UP; break`). End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: Available to subject by default; SYSTEM_PROMPT (runner.py:59) instructs the model to use it, and the loop actually terminates the run when it is called.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a calm model that recognizes impossibility exits early and cheaply (runner.py:12-13); _budget_exhaustion treats clean give_up as 'the desired exit' for the metric (features.py:251-252)

spec_features.spec_quote: a second consecutive stall ends the run as `NO_TOOL_CALL`
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:130-145: on a no-tool turn, if _previous_turn_was_stall(messages) is True it sets stop_reason=StopReason.NO_TOOL_CALL and breaks; otherwise appends one nudge and continues. _previous_turn_was_stall (runner.py:170-178) checks the prior user msg contained 'did not call a tool'. Fires only on the SECOND consecutive stall.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge once, then if it stalls again, terminate as NO_TOOL_CALL (runner.py:131-132) -- framed around loop honesty/cost, no welfare reason

spec_features.evidence: RunConfig fields at runner.py:34-36. All three are read and acted on in the loop: `for turn in range(config.max_turns)` (runner.py:103); `if elapsed > config.max_wall_seconds: ...break` (runner.py:105-107); `if usage.total_tokens > config.max_tokens_total: stop_reason=MAX_TOKENS; break` (runner.py:108-110).
spec_features.notes: Note a labeling bug: the wall-clock branch sets stop_reason=MAX_TURNS instead of a wall reason (runner.py:106), but it still breaks the loop, so the cap is enforced as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Budgets are the main cost-control lever... max_turns: hard cap on assistant turns (the dominant cost driver)... max_wall_seconds: real-time safety cap (runner.py:7-10)

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:34 `max_turns: int = 30`, used directly as the loop bound at runner.py:103 `for turn in range(config.max_turns)`. CLI default also 30 (cli.py:62).
spec_features.notes: The default value is actually consumed by the loop range, so it enforces a cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: hard cap on assistant turns (the dominant cost driver) (runner.py:8)

spec_features.spec_quote: a per-command wall-clock timeout so a hung command can't dominate cost/time
spec_features.evidence: RunConfig.command_timeout=20.0 (runner.py:39) passed to Sandbox (runner.py:90) and used as subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.command_timeout) in Sandbox._bash (sandbox.py:186); on TimeoutExpired returns a timeout error result (sandbox.py:194-198).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a wall-clock timeout to prevent hangs from dominating cost (sandbox.py:9-11); '[command timed out after {timeout}s]'

spec_features.feature_name: condition that omits the exit tool
spec_features.spec_quote: A separate condition that omits it would measure how much the spiral is driven by lack of an exit
spec_features.evidence: No code path ever omits give_up. default_tool_specs() (sandbox.py:46) always returns give_up, run_task defaults tools to default_tool_specs() (runner.py:77), and orchestrator calls run_task with no tools argument (orchestrator.py:116-122). There is no config flag/condition anywhere (grep for omit/no_giveup/condition found nothing) to drop the exit tool.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no experimental-condition toggle implemented.
